additions.name: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology — Changwang Building Data Centre

status.summary: Nanjing University of Information Science and Technology operates a campus hosting room on the first floor of Changwang Building. On September 18, its information and data-management centre asked university units to review unused, powered-off and overdue hosted equipment to reclaim room space and electrical capacity while allowing approved hosting to continue. The September 24 collection deadline does not establish that this equipment review was completed.

locator.precision: Representative point inside the community-mapped Changwang Building at NUIST’s Nanjing campus. It identifies the host building, not the first-floor data-centre room footprint, an entrance or a surveyed parcel.
locator.identity_review: The September 18 university operator notice explicitly places the data-centre room on Changwang Building’s first floor. The official 2023 university event notice identifies Changwang at 219 Ningliu Road; the official service directory independently identifies the building in the central campus area (Zhongyuan). Native OSM way 1114839561 has the exact Chinese building name 长望楼. Every building vertex is inside outer way 93553391 of the university-named relation 13070911, rather than the separate southern Yuyuan component 1057168425. The 2024 building changeset also explicitly describes NUIST Zhongyuan. The contact office S103 and event hall N102 are not assigned as the data-centre room.
locator.uncertainty_reason: Community mapping provides no measured horizontal accuracy or verified first-floor room footprint. Decimal coordinate precision is not survey accuracy.

additions.successor_review: September 18 is the visible and signed operator-notice date and the operational observation. Existing hosting management and continued-hosting approval support the operational classification; the idle/powered-off equipment subset is not treated as the condition of the whole facility. Bounded exact-room, current-year and clearance successor searches found the September 18 original and no verified later completion or closure. September 24 is only a scheduled collection deadline. The undated public hosting-service page supplies policy context, not a fresh date. No historical HPC or other campus capacity is transferred.

additions.site_name: Shaanxi Xueqian Normal University Chang’an Campus Data Centre
additions.name: Shaanxi Xueqian Normal University — Chang’an Data Centre Room Renovation

status.summary: A September 9 university inspection confirmed completion of the summer renovation of the data-centre room and its power room. The work concerns the existing facility in Jixue Building A102 on Chang’an campus. Procurement documents described 16 existing IT cabinets and upgrades to cooling, cold-aisle containment, electrical distribution and fire protection; the exact day the renovation finished was not reported.

locator.precision: Representative point inside Shaanxi Xueqian Normal University’s Chang’an campus at 101 Shenhe Second Road. It locates the named parent campus, not Jixue Building, room A102, an entrance or a surveyed parcel.
locator.identity_review: The original full procurement document identifies the data-centre room as Jixue Building A102. The official university campus-map page groups the illustration naming Jixue Building under Chang’an campus and separately identifies Yanta campus. Its footer gives Chang’an as 101 Shenhe Second Road. Native OSM way 246285562 exactly names Chang’an campus, with the same street and house number. This is a named campus/address bridge, not a university-name or road-intersection guess.
locator.uncertainty_reason: Community map geometry provides no measured positional accuracy. Displacement from this campus point to room A102 is unknown.

additions.successor_review: The September 9 physical inspection confirms a completed renovation, reported September 11. It does not date the actual summer completion day, original opening, or item-by-item acceptance. The original full tender identifies the room and historical existing cabinets; the June award alone is not physical-work evidence. One room entry covers the associated power-room work. The separate Information Engineering College AI-compute plans are excluded. Bounded exact-title/domain searches and captured university IT home/overview found no later contradictory facility report. A May failed first procurement was followed by the documented second-round award, so it is not treated as cancellation of the renovation.
